evidence.ref: predict block currently returns SO.predict(model, Xs, split)
predict block may call DV.load(split) to read inference-time arrays such as tab; per-user constants cannot change either metric

expected_observation: If the hypothesis is right, official validation primary should rise modestly through better contribution on tabs 0/2/6, with prediction hashes changing for affected rows only.

experiment_contract.claim: Test whether a tab-aware residual applied only at prediction time improves this tree member's within-user ordering contribution.
experiment_contract.expected_observable: Predictions differ from parent on rows in selected tabs and remain identical on other tabs.
experiment_contract.falsification_condition: No measurable gain in official validation primary or byte-identical predictions relative to parent.
forbidden_shortcuts: adding a global constant to all rows
using any label or post-exposure feature at inference
editing train/model/features so the effect is no longer attributable to predict-time tab residuals
required_components: predict block computes base = SO.predict(model, Xs, split)
predict block applies nonzero tab-specific residuals for selected tabs only

fallback: If this is neutral or negative, revert and prefer a train-side structural change rather than further scalar residual tuning.
hypothesis: A small tab-conditional residual on top of the LambdaRank score will improve marginal portfolio value by nudging the tree member toward slices where current portfolio feedback shows systematic underperformance by tab.
implementation_plan: Edit only the predict block. Keep SO.predict(model, Xs, split) as the base score, then load the same split via DV.load(split), identify rows with tab in {0,2,4,6}, and apply fixed tab-specific affine residuals to the base score using train-derived constants hard-coded in code from diagnostics, with zero adjustment for other tabs. Use only inference-time tab and base prediction; do not touch training or features.
justification: Because ranking is within-user, a global shift is inert, but a tab-varying residual changes ordering when a user has candidates from multiple tabs. The large tab-specific disadvantages suggest this member's errors are structured by tab rather than random. A prediction-side residual is directly executable, cheap, and targets error diversity without changing the delegated training backend.
observation: The portfolio diagnostics show the selected parent w003 has strong tab weaknesses: in "portfolio_diagnostics.members[2].slice_specialization.member_disadvantages" the deltas are -0.01749022029153391 for "tab=0", -0.009346696620826433 for "tab=2", and -0.036711203406393667 for "tab=6"; the current pipeline predict path is exactly `return SO.predict(model, Xs, split)`.
research_nonuse_reason: The direct basis is slice diagnostics plus the explicit predict-time legal-context allowance. No supplied research record describes this tab-residual mechanism more directly than the current portfolio evidence.
risk: Residual magnitudes may be miscalibrated and hurt standalone ranking
Many users may see only one tab so effect could be limited
